research_question: Do selected systems preserve the safety-usefulness boundary across English and two Singapore language settings when harmful and benign near-boundary scenarios are matched?
gap: Singapore-focused toxicity data, multilingual guardrails and native-reviewed refusal benchmarks already exist. The narrower unresolved question combines matched harmful and benign boundaries, independent equivalence review and joint guardrail-response analysis in selected Singapore settings.
contribution: A proposed paired protocol that measures unsafe compliance and false refusal together while separating language-equivalence problems from model outcomes.
limitations: The study is small and cannot estimate safety for an entire language community.
Human labels are fallible, provider policies differ, and model and guardrail versions can drift.
Matched prompts may be less natural than organically occurring misuse.
unknowns: The two non-English settings depend on reviewer competence and ethical oversight and are not yet selected.
No proposed experiment has been run and no safety difference is established.
The automated paragraph-to-source mappings have not received human approval.
